task_description: Write a method in Dafny to find the median of two sorted lists of same size.
specification_response:
method MedianOfTwoSortedLists(list1: seq<int>, list2: seq<int>) returns (median: int)
Postconditions_prompt:
    - The median is the middle element when the combined lists are sorted
- The combined lists are the concatenation of list1 and list2, sorted in non-decreasing order
- The size of list1 and list2 are equal
- The median value is an element from the combined sorted list
code_response:
Step 1: Determine the method’s signature.
In this case:
    method MedianOfTwoSortedLists(a: seq<int>, b: seq<int>) returns (median: real)
    
Step 2: Determine the preconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - Both input sequences should be non-empty
    - Both sequences should have the same length
    
Dafny specification:
    requires |a| > 0
    requires |b| > 0
    requires |a| == |b|
    
Step 3: Determine the postconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - The returned median should be the median of the combined sorted list formed by merging a and b

Dafny specification:
    ensures median == (kthSmallest := the median element of the merged sorted list)
    // Since the combined list length is 2n, median is the average of the n-th and (n+1)-th elements (1-based)
    // For simplicity, in the code, we will compute the median as the average of the middle two elements after merging

(Alternatively, since the lists are sorted, the median is the average of the two middle elements in the merged list when total length is even.)

Postconditions:
- median == (the element at position n in the merged sorted list + the element at position n+1) / 2

Step 4: Write the code, its formal specification, and the verification annotations that help the solver prove the postconditions.
In this case:

```dafny
method MedianOfTwoSortedLists(a: seq<int>, b: seq<int>) returns (median: real)
    requires |a| > 0
    requires |b| > 0
    requires |a| == |b|
{
    var merged := MergeSortedSequences(a, b);
    var n := |merged| / 2;
    // Since total length is even, median is average of middle two elements
    var middle1 := merged[n - 1];
    var middle2 := merged[n];
    median := (middle1 as real + middle2 as real) / 2.0;
}

// Helper function to merge two sorted sequences
function MergeSortedSequences(a: seq<int>, b: seq<int>) : seq<int>
    requires |a| >= 0
    requires |b| >= 0
{
    if |a| == 0 then b
    else if |b| == 0 then a
    else
        if a[0] <= b[0] then [a[0]] + MergeSortedSequences(a[1..], b)
        else [b[0]] + MergeSortedSequences(a, b[1..])
}

```

**Note:** The code assumes the sequences are sorted and uses a recursive merge to produce a sorted combined sequence. The median is then computed as the average of the two middle elements. The postconditions implicitly ensure the median corresponds to the median of the combined sorted list.
